name: HOT PLATE
desc: Heavy-Duty Rectangular Laboratory Hot Plate engineered for uniform thermal heating and sample preparation workflows. Features a robust 12-inch heavy cast iron heating plate reaching surface temperatures up to 300°C.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS HOT PLATE is a heavy-duty rectangular laboratory heating device engineered for uniform thermal processing of samples, media, and reagents. Its robust 12-inch cast iron plate provides excellent thermal conductivity and heat retention, achieving surface temperatures up to 300°C with a precision energy regulator for incremental control. This hot plate is indispensable in clinical, academic, and industrial laboratories for applications such as boiling and evaporation of aqueous and organic solvents, acid digestion of samples using strong acids like hydrochloric acid (HCl), nitric acid (HNO3), and sulfuric acid (H2SO4), melting and sterilization of microbiological culture media (e.g., agar, broth), and general sample preparation for B.Sc/M.Sc students, PhD researchers, and analytical chemists. It supports compliance with standard testing protocols such as ASTM and ISO methods for thermal stability, residue analysis, and dissolution testing, ensuring reproducible and safe heating in fume hoods and open bench environments.
sop: Place the hot plate on a stable, level, heat-resistant surface away from flammable materials and ensure adequate ventilation (e.g., in a fume hood if working with volatile chemicals).
Connect the power cord to a properly grounded 220V, 50Hz electrical outlet and switch on the main power supply; the pilot lamp will illuminate.
Press the 'SET' button once on the precision energy regulator to enter temperature setpoint mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target temperature (e.g., 100°C for boiling water, 150°C for gentle evaporation, or up to 300°C for high-temperature digestions).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value; the controller will now heat the plate to the setpoint and maintain it.
Allow the plate to preheat for 5-10 minutes until the surface reaches the desired temperature; verify with an external thermometer or thermocouple if precise temperature is critical.

Place the sample container (beaker, flask, or crucible) centrally on the hot plate using appropriate thermal-resistant gloves or tongs; ensure the container is compatible with the temperature and chemical being heated.
Monitor the heating process continuously; for boiling or evaporation, adjust the setpoint as needed by repeating steps 3-5.
After the heating task is complete, turn off the hot plate by switching off the main power supply and unplugging the unit.
Allow the cast iron plate to cool to room temperature before cleaning; never touch the plate surface while hot.
Clean the cooled plate with a mild detergent or appropriate solvent, avoiding abrasive materials that could damage the surface; wipe dry with a soft cloth.

Safety Warning: Never heat flammable solvents or volatile organic compounds on an open hot plate without a fume hood and spark-proof environment; always use a water bath or heating mantle for such applications to prevent fire or explosion. Additionally, do not leave the hot plate unattended during operation, and always wear heat-resistant gloves and safety goggles.
